title: Understanding Tags
learningGoal: Understand what a tag is, how it helps, and when another part of LeadProspectrr is a better choice.

items.title: A Short Label
items.description: A tag is a short label attached to a contact. Think of tags as labels on folders. The label helps you find a group of people who share something in common.

items.title: Examples
items.description: INT-Coaching, ACT-Booked-Call, STS-Qualified. One contact can have several tags telling a short story without reading every note.

items.title: Find and Filter
items.description: Search for contacts, filter contacts, build Smart Lists.

items.title: Communication
items.description: Select recipients for email or SMS campaigns.

items.title: Automation
items.description: Start a workflow, guide contacts through workflow paths, record meaningful actions.

items.title: Not a Replacement
items.description: Tags should not replace every other part of the CRM. Use the right tool for each job.

items.title: Best Place for Information
items.description: Shared label to group people: Tag. Details like budget or renewal date: Custom field. Broad relationship like lead or client: Contact type. Sales deal steps: Pipeline stage. Background info: Note. Reminders: Task.

keyPoint: Tags are short labels that group contacts. Use them for what they do best, and use other CRM features for details, deals, notes, and tasks.

actionSteps.title: Review Your Current Tags
actionSteps.description: Look at tags you currently use. Are any being used for things better suited to fields, pipelines, or notes?

actionSteps.title: Identify Misused Tags
actionSteps.description: Find tags storing details that should be custom fields, or tracking deals that should be in pipelines.

actionSteps.title: Plan Corrections
actionSteps.description: Decide which tags to keep, which to convert to other features, and which to delete.

quizzes.question: What is the main purpose of a tag?

options.option_text: To store detailed contact information like budget amounts
To group contacts using a shared label for finding, filtering, and automation
To replace all other CRM features
To send emails directly without workflows

quizzes.explanation: Tags are short labels that group contacts who share something in common. They help with finding, filtering, communication, and automation—but they don't replace other CRM features like custom fields or pipelines.

quizzes.question: Where should you store a prospect's budget information?

options.option_text: In a tag like Budget-5000
In a custom field
In the contact's first name
In a workflow name

quizzes.explanation: Budget information belongs in a custom field, not a tag. Creating tags for every budget range creates too many tags and makes the list unmanageable.

quizzes.question: Where should you track a deal moving from Proposal Sent to Contract Signed?

options.option_text: Using tags like STS-Proposal-Sent and STS-Contract-Signed
In the opportunity pipeline
In the contact's email address
In a note only

quizzes.explanation: Sales deal stages belong in the opportunity pipeline, not tags. Pipelines are designed to track deals moving through defined steps with values and statuses.

title: Build a Simple Tagging Structure
learningGoal: Create a shared naming structure that makes each tag easy to understand.

items.title: INT- = Interest
items.description: What does this person care about? Examples: INT-Speaking, INT-Executive-Coaching, INT-Consulting.

items.title: ACT- = Action
items.description: What has this person done? Examples: ACT-Downloaded-Guide, ACT-Booked-Call, ACT-Attended-Clinic.

items.title: STS- = Status
items.description: Where does this person currently stand? Examples: STS-New-Lead, STS-Qualified, STS-Client.

items.title: What They Care About
items.description: Interest tags identify the topic, service, programme, or offer that matters to the contact. A contact can have multiple Interest tags.

items.title: Examples
items.description: Speaker: INT-Keynote and INT-Workshop. Coach: INT-One-to-One-Coaching and INT-Group-Coaching.

items.title: What They Did
items.description: Action tags record meaningful behaviour. Most useful when the action changes what should happen next.

items.title: Good Examples
items.description: ACT-Downloaded-Guide, ACT-Attended-Clinic, ACT-Booked-Call, ACT-Requested-Proposal.

items.title: Avoid Over-Tagging
items.description: Avoid creating tags for every small activity. Hundreds of tags for email opens make the list harder to use.

items.title: Where They Stand
items.description: Status tags describe the contact's current position. Require tighter control than Interest and Action tags.

items.title: Examples
items.description: STS-New-Lead, STS-Qualified, STS-Client, STS-Inactive.

items.title: Changing Status
items.description: When status changes: 1) Remove old Status tag. 2) Add new Status tag. A person should not normally be both STS-New-Lead and STS-Client.

items.title: Good Pattern
items.description: PREFIX-Clear-Description. Examples: INT-Speaking, ACT-Booked-Call, STS-Qualified.

items.title: Avoid These
items.description: speaker interest, Interested in speaking, Booked call 2026, Hot!!!, Follow up sometime. Problems: different formats, dates in tags, opinion-based labels, vague wording.

keyPoint: Use the three-part model: INT- for Interest, ACT- for Action, STS- for Status. Follow the PREFIX-Clear-Description naming pattern. Avoid duplicates, dates, and vague labels.

actionSteps.title: Choose Your Service
actionSteps.description: Pick one service or offer from your business.

actionSteps.title: Create Three Tags
actionSteps.description: Create one INT- tag, one ACT- tag, and one STS- tag for that service.

actionSteps.title: Check Naming
actionSteps.description: Verify each tag follows PREFIX-Clear-Description format.

quizzes.question: Which prefix is used for an Interest tag?

options.option_text: ACT-
INT-
STS-
TAG-

quizzes.explanation: INT- is the prefix for Interest tags. ACT- is for Action tags, and STS- is for Status tags.

quizzes.question: What should you do when a contact's status changes from New Lead to Qualified?

options.option_text: Keep both STS-New-Lead and STS-Qualified tags
Remove STS-New-Lead and add STS-Qualified
Delete all tags and start over
Only add STS-Qualified without removing anything

quizzes.explanation: When status changes, remove the old Status tag and add the new one. A contact should not normally have multiple conflicting Status tags.

quizzes.question: Which tag best records that someone booked a call?

options.option_text: INT-Booked-Call
ACT-Booked-Call
STS-Booked-Call
Booked call 2026

quizzes.explanation: ACT-Booked-Call is correct because booking a call is an action the contact took. Avoid putting dates in tags like Booked call 2026.

title: Add and Remove Tags
learningGoal: Apply tags correctly to individual contacts and groups of contacts.

sections.title: Add a Tag to One Contact

items.title: Steps
items.description: 1. Open Contacts. 2. Search for the contact. 3. Open contact record. 4. Find Tags area. 5. Select existing tag or type new approved name. 6. Confirm tag appears.

sections.title: Remove a Tag from One Contact

items.title: Steps
items.description: 1. Open contact record. 2. Find tag to remove. 3. Select removal option. 4. Confirm tag disappeared. Removing a tag does not delete the contact or their information.

items.title: Add Tags to Several Contacts
items.description: 1. Open Contacts. 2. Filter if needed. 3. Select contacts with checkboxes. 4. Choose Add Tags from bulk action bar. 5. Select tags. 6. Enter clear action name. 7. Submit. 8. Review results.

items.title: Remove Tags from Several Contacts
items.description: 1. Select contacts. 2. Choose Remove Tags. 3. Select exact tag(s). 4. Give action clear name. 5. Submit. 6. Review results.

items.title: Remove All Tags Warning
items.description: Use Remove all tags only when goal is to clear every tag from selected contacts. Bulk removal has no one-click undo.

items.title: Safe Bulk Process
items.description: Before bulk change: Filter carefully. Review several records. Confirm number selected. Apply exact tag. Check results. Open contacts to confirm.

keyPoint: Add and remove tags one at a time or in bulk. Use safe processes for bulk changes. Remember: removing a tag does not delete the contact.

actionSteps.title: Create Test Contact
actionSteps.description: Create a test contact called Jamie Example.

actionSteps.title: Add Tags
actionSteps.description: Add your INT- tag, ACT- tag, and STS-New-Lead tag.

actionSteps.title: Change Status
actionSteps.description: Remove STS-New-Lead and add STS-Qualified. Confirm only correct Status tag remains.

nextLessonTitle: Find Contacts with Tags and Smart Lists

quizzes.question: What happens when you remove a tag from a contact?

options.option_text: The contact and all their data are deleted
Only the tag is removed; the contact and their information remain
All tags are removed from the contact
The contact's email address is deleted

quizzes.explanation: Removing a tag only removes that label from the contact. The contact record, messages, notes, and all other information remain intact.

quizzes.question: What is the risk of using Remove all tags in bulk?

options.option_text: It only removes one selected tag
It clears every tag from selected contacts with no one-click undo
It deletes the selected contacts
It automatically adds new tags

quizzes.explanation: Remove all tags clears every tag from the selected contacts, not just one. There is no one-click undo, so you must know which contacts should receive which tags again.

quizzes.question: What should you do before applying a bulk tag change?

options.option_text: Apply the change immediately to all contacts
Filter carefully, review records, confirm number selected, then apply
Delete all existing tags first
Send an email to all contacts first

quizzes.explanation: Before bulk tagging, filter carefully, review several records from the result, confirm the number of selected contacts, apply the exact tag, check results, and open contacts to confirm the change.

title: Find Contacts with Tags and Smart Lists
learningGoal: Turn tags into useful contact groups that can be found and reused.

items.title: Steps
items.description: 1. Open Contacts or Smart Lists. 2. Open Advanced Filters. 3. Search for Tag filter. 4. Select condition. 5. Choose tag (e.g., INT-Coaching). 6. Apply filter.

items.title: Example
items.description: Find qualified contacts interested in coaching: Use INT-Coaching AND STS-Qualified.

items.title: Match All vs Match Any
items.description: Match all returns people with BOTH tags. Match any returns people with at least ONE of the tags.

items.title: Steps
items.description: 1. Confirm filter produces correct contacts. 2. Save filtered view as Smart List. 3. Give it a clear name (e.g., Qualified Coaching Prospects).

items.title: Smart List Behavior
items.description: A Smart List is a saved view. Contacts appear or disappear as their information changes.

items.title: Speakers
items.description: Meeting planners interested in keynotes. Prospects who requested speaker packet. Qualified contacts who have not booked.

items.title: Coaches
items.description: People interested in group coaching. Assessment completers who have not booked. Current clients interested in new programme.

items.title: Consultants
items.description: Qualified CRM prospects. People who requested proposal. Past clients interested in ongoing support.

keyPoint: Filter contacts by tags, combine multiple tag conditions, and save useful combinations as Smart Lists. Smart Lists update automatically as contact information changes.

actionSteps.title: Filter by Tag
actionSteps.description: Find everyone with your INT- tag.

actionSteps.title: Combine Filters
actionSteps.description: Add STS-Qualified condition and set to Match all.

actionSteps.title: Save Smart List
actionSteps.description: Save with a clear name like Qualified Coaching Prospects.

quizzes.question: What is the difference between Match all and Match any when combining tag filters?

options.option_text: There is no difference
Match all returns people with BOTH tags; Match any returns people with at least ONE tag
Match all deletes contacts; Match any saves them
Match all is slower than Match any

quizzes.explanation: Match all returns contacts who have every specified tag. Match any returns contacts who have at least one of the specified tags. Choose based on whether you need all conditions or any condition.

quizzes.question: What does a Smart List do?

options.option_text: It creates a static list that never changes
It saves a filtered view that updates as contacts meet or stop meeting conditions
It deletes contacts that don't match
It sends emails automatically

quizzes.explanation: A Smart List is a saved, dynamic view. Contacts automatically appear when they meet the conditions and disappear when they no longer meet them.

quizzes.question: When should you save a filtered view as a Smart List?

options.option_text: Only if you will never use it again
When the filtered group will be used again
Only for deleted contacts
Never, Smart Lists are not useful

quizzes.explanation: Save a filtered view as a Smart List when you will use that group of contacts repeatedly. This saves time and ensures the list stays current.

title: Use Tags with Workflows
learningGoal: Start and update simple automations based on contact tags.

items.title: Example
items.description: Send follow-up after someone downloads a guide.

items.title: Steps
items.description: 1. Open Automations → Workflows. 2. Create or open workflow. 3. Add Trigger. 4. Choose Contact Tag. 5. Set to Tag Added. 6. Select ACT-Downloaded-Guide. 7. Add actions. 8. Save. 9. Test. 10. Publish.

items.title: Example
items.description: Removing STS-Client could start an offboarding process.

items.title: Important
items.description: Before using tag-removal trigger, define exactly why the tag would be removed and what should happen next.

sections.title: Add or Remove Tags Inside Workflow

items.title: Add Contact Tag Action
items.description: Use when automation should label the contact. Example: Contact submits form → Workflow sends confirmation → Workflow adds ACT-Completed-Assessment.

items.title: Remove Contact Tag Action
items.description: Use when tag is no longer correct. Example: Contact becomes qualified → Workflow removes STS-New-Lead → Workflow adds STS-Qualified.

items.title: Be Careful
items.description: Be careful when one workflow adds a tag that triggers another workflow, especially if the second workflow adds the original tag again.

items.title: Before Publishing
items.description: Write down which tag starts each workflow. List every tag added or removed. Check whether another workflow reacts to those changes. Test with one contact. Review workflow history.

keyPoint: Use Contact Tag triggers to start workflows when tags are added or removed. Use Add/Remove Contact Tag actions inside workflows. Always check for potential loops before publishing.

actionSteps.title: Create Tag Workflow
actionSteps.description: Create workflow with trigger: Contact Tag Added: ACT-Downloaded-Guide.

actionSteps.title: Add Actions
actionSteps.description: Send guide email, wait one day, send follow-up question, add task for personal follow-up.

actionSteps.title: Test and Check
actionSteps.description: Test with one contact. Check for loops. Review workflow history.

quizzes.question: Which workflow trigger responds when a tag is added or removed?

options.option_text: Form Submitted
Contact Tag
Appointment Booked
Payment Received

quizzes.explanation: The Contact Tag trigger can start workflows when a tag is added or removed. Set the event to Tag Added or Tag Removed and select the specific tag.

quizzes.question: What should you do before publishing a workflow that adds or removes tags?

options.option_text: Publish immediately without checking
Check for workflow loops by reviewing which tags trigger which workflows
Delete all existing tags
Create duplicate workflows

quizzes.explanation: Before publishing, write down which tag starts each workflow, list every tag added or removed, check whether another workflow reacts to those changes, test with one contact, and review the workflow history.

quizzes.question: In what order should you remove and add Status tags in a workflow?

options.option_text: Add new tag first, then remove old tag
Remove old tag first, then add new tag
Only add new tag without removing old one
Remove both tags and add nothing

quizzes.explanation: The removal action should come before the new Status tag is added. This reduces the chance of conflicting Status tags existing at the same time.

title: Keep the Tag List Clean
learningGoal: Review existing tags and reduce confusion without breaking active processes.

items.title: Look For
items.description: Duplicate tags with different spellings. Tags with no clear meaning. Old event or campaign tags no longer needed. Conflicting Status tags. Tags used as notes. Tags containing dates. Tags from old integrations. Tags no current process uses.

items.title: Duplicate Example
items.description: INT-Coaching, Coaching Interest, interested-coaching, Coach Lead. These may describe the same group. Choose one approved tag.

items.title: Where Tags May Be Connected
items.description: Workflow triggers, workflow actions, Smart Lists, campaign filters, forms and surveys, contact imports, third-party connections, reports, manual processes.

items.title: Important
items.description: Do not rename or delete a tag until you know where it is being used.

items.title: 10-Step Process
items.description: 1. Export current tag list. 2. Group into Interest, Action, Status, Other. 3. Mark duplicates. 4. Identify tag name to remain. 5. Check every process using old tags. 6. Apply approved tag to correct contacts. 7. Update workflows, filters, campaigns. 8. Remove old tags from contacts. 9. Delete old tags only after checks complete. 10. Record approved naming rules.

items.title: Keep a Simple List
items.description: Track: Tag name, Group, Meaning, Added by, Used in, Review status. This helps future users understand and maintain the tagging system.

keyPoint: Regularly review tags for duplicates and unclear names. Check where tags are used before changing them. Follow a safe cleanup process. Maintain a tag register.

actionSteps.title: Audit Five Tags
actionSteps.description: Choose five tags and answer: What does it mean? What group? Any duplicates? Where used? Keep, rename, merge, or remove?

actionSteps.title: Start Tag Register
actionSteps.description: Create a simple list of approved tags with their group, meaning, and where used.

actionSteps.title: Plan Cleanup
actionSteps.description: Identify which tags need attention but do not delete live tags until all connected processes are checked.

quizzes.question: What should you check before renaming or deleting a tag?

options.option_text: Nothing, just delete it immediately
Workflows, Smart Lists, campaigns, forms, imports, integrations, and reports that use the tag
Only the tag color
Whether it is the oldest tag

quizzes.explanation: Before renaming or deleting a tag, check every place it might be used: workflow triggers and actions, Smart Lists, campaign filters, forms, imports, third-party connections, reports, and manual processes.

quizzes.question: What is the first step in the tag cleanup process?

options.option_text: Immediately delete all old tags
Export or record the current tag list
Create new tags without checking existing ones
Rename everything at once

quizzes.explanation: The first step is to export or record the current tag list. This gives you a complete picture before making any changes.

quizzes.question: Why should you maintain a tag register?

options.option_text: It is required by law
It helps future users understand what each tag means and where it is used
It makes tags automatically apply to contacts
It deletes old tags automatically

quizzes.explanation: A tag register documents approved tags, their meanings, and where they are used. This helps team members understand and maintain the tagging system consistently.
